messages:
cheng: quick follow-up from the RFC review — we need a concrete plan for handling partial streaming responses + retries when the client reconnects mid-stream. current notes are a bit fuzzy on who owns fragmenting and resume semantics.

julia: agreed. two options I sketched: 1) gateway fragments and emits resume-tokens, client reconnects and asks gateway to resend from token; 2) client-side chunking with monotonic chunk-ids that the gateway uses for dedupe.

mike: pros/cons? gateway-fragmenting centralizes policy but needs memory or spooling. client-chunking pushes complexity to clients we don't control.

sarah: also think about connection types: HTTP/2, HTTP/3 vs websocket. resumability semantics differ a lot. we should design an abstract fragment model that maps to each protocol.

julia: yep. proposal: canonical "fragment" is a logical piece of output with a stable fragment-id + optional resume-token. fragments are the unit of retry and dedupe.

cheng: sounds good. details: what does a fragment header look like? minimal fields: fragment-id, seq, resume-token (opaque), checksum, final-bit. e.g.
```
fragment-id: 000123
seq: 42
resume-token: rtk_xxx
checksum: sha256:ab12...
final: false
```

mike: who issues the resume-token? gateway or runtime? if gateway issues it, it has to track mapping to backend KV cache for some window. that adds state.

julia: runtime can generate tokens but gateway stores only short-lived pointers. token is opaque to client; gateway/runtimes validate it. expiry window configurable by tenant.

sarah: memory budget: we need a spool-to-disk fallback. for Dedicated customers with high throughput, we can't keep N minutes of fragments in RAM. propose LRU spool + guaranteed in-memory window for low-latency clients.

olivia: what about semantics for partial success? e.g., first N fragments delivered, later fragments fail — should clients treat stream as completed or retry-and-append? product asks for predictable behavior.

cheng: API-level rule: stream is "append-only" until a terminal fragment (final: true) is emitted. If client reconnects with a resume-token, gateway must guarantee exactly-once delivery per fragment-id within the token window. outside window, gateway responds with new-request suggestion (client should restart).

julia: dedupe logic: fragment-id must be globally unique per request (e.g., request-id + seq). gateway checks fragment-id seen set keyed by request-id. small bloom filter + persistent marker for spool can reduce memory.

mike: how about mid-fragment failures? if client disconnects mid-fragment, do we resume inside a fragment or only at fragment boundaries? resuming inside fragment complicates kernels and KV cache.

sarah: I'd avoid intra-fragment resume initially. require fragments small-ish (<= 64KB) so retransmit cost is bounded. we can revisit if embeddings/large-binary payloads show need.

julia: another tradeoff: use HTTP trailers to carry final fragment metadata vs inline header per fragment. trailers are nice for finality but not supported everywhere. inline header per fragment is safer.

cheng: ops: need visibility. add trace events: fragment-emitted, fragment-acked, fragment-resend, token-issued, token-expired. expose counts in console.

mike: rollout plan: implement fragment-id + token support in gateway proxy first with in-memory window + boolean feature flag, test with small beta customers. runtime integration next to emit fragment metadata.

olivia: +1 for gradual rollout. can we expose a compatibility mode where clients can opt into strict exactly-once vs at-least-once? some customers prefer simpler semantics.

julia: we can surface that as a per-route config: resume_policy = {exactly_once, best_effort}. default = best_effort for hosted, exactly_once for Dedicated by opt-in.

sarah: edge case: multi-region failover. token must encode region or be universally resolvable. otherwise resume will fail when routed to different region. tokens should be globally verifiable by control plane or include signed metadata.

cheng: action items: 1) julia to draft fragment header and token format (RFC) by EOD Thu. 2) mike to prototype gateway state window + LRU spool by next week. 3) sarah to write SLO/memory impact doc for ops. 4) olivia to collect product requirements for resume policies.

deploy-bot: draft rfc created: /rfc/stream-resume-token-v0 (link) :white_check_mark:

mike: quick question — should resume-token include a HMAC to prevent tampering? makes it verifiable without lookup.

julia: yes include short HMAC + validity window. still need mapping to spool location in some cases. token structure: base64(payload).hmac where payload={request_id, last_seq, issued_at, region, flags}.

cheng: great. keep thread narrow on implementation details in next RFC iteration. thanks all.
